introduction: On this Sunday, the Book of Wisdom praises God, who judges with gentleness and gives his children hope through repentance. In the Gospel, Jesus tells parables of the Kingdom: the weeds among the wheat, which grow together until the harvest, the mustard seed and the yeast. Paul tells us that the Spirit helps us in our weakness and prays within us. Let us be patient, as God is patient with us.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, the Lord is good and forgiving, rich in mercy to all who call on him. Let us bring him our prayers.
intentions: For the Church: that she may be patient and merciful, leaving final judgment to God. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who are discouraged by the evil in the world: that they may trust in God's harvest. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who have done wrong: that God, who gives repentance, may lead them to conversion. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who do not know how to pray: that the Holy Spirit may pray within them. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that we may be like yeast in the world, quietly spreading the goodness of the Kingdom. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Lord God, you are patient with us and give us time to repent. Teach us to be patient with others, and let your Kingdom grow in us like a small seed. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: Let both grow together
reflection.body:
The Book of Wisdom praises the way God uses his power: "But you, being sovereign in strength, judge in gentleness, and with great forbearance you govern us." God is strong enough to be patient. And through this patience he teaches his people "how the righteous must be kind," and gives them hope, "because you give repentance when men have sinned."

In the Gospel, Jesus tells a parable about a farmer who sows good seed, but an enemy comes at night and sows weeds among the wheat. When the servants discover the weeds, they want to pull them up at once. The master says no: "lest perhaps while you gather up the darnel weeds, you root up the wheat with them. Let both grow together until the harvest."

This parable speaks to a question many people ask: why does God allow evil to continue? Jesus' answer is that the final separation belongs to God, at the end of time. Until then, good and evil grow together, in the world and even in each of us. We are not to rush to judge and condemn. God is patient, giving every person time to change.

Jesus tells two more short parables. The Kingdom is like a tiny mustard seed that grows into a tree where birds can rest. And it is like yeast that a woman mixes into flour, "until it was all leavened." The Kingdom often grows quietly and invisibly, transforming everything from within.

Paul offers comfort for our own weakness: "the Spirit also helps our weaknesses, for we don't know how to pray as we ought. But the Spirit himself makes intercession for us with groanings which can't be uttered."

This week, notice where you are quick to judge others, and leave the judgment to God. Be patient with yourself too. And be a little yeast: a quiet influence for good where you live and work.
